---
title: Create True-Shape Links
subtitle: Redissolving candidate centerlines and splitting only at snapped model nodes to produce true-shape link pieces
description: CandidateTDMRoadLinks is fully re-dissolved into maximal topological chains per VERT_LEVEL (undoing incidental arcpy junction cuts; level isolation prevents GEOS from spuriously noding elevated roads against at-grade crossings), then same-route chains split only by an incidental level boundary (e.g. a freeway climbing onto its own flyover) are restitched, then the result is split only at snapped WFRC road model-node positions to produce the raw building-block pieces for true-shape link conflation. CC attachment and external station nodes are excluded from this split (folded in separately later). Lineage/display attributes (OBJECTID, UNIQUE_ID, DOT_FCLASS, VERT_LEVEL, etc.) are reattached onto each piece via a midpoint-nearest join against CandidateTDMRoadLinks — VERT_LEVEL there is informational only, not a matching key.

## Setup

### Imports

```{python}
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from shapely.geometry import Point

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
from _src.link_utils import resolve_snap_coords, split_candidate_links
from _src.centerline_utils import (
    dissolve_and_singlepart,
    restitch_vert_level_transitions,
    transfer_attributes_by_midpoint,
)
```

### Configuration

```{python}
# ── Filepaths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PATHS = {
    "in_centerlines":  Path("_data/processed/CandidateTDMRoadLinks.gpkg"),
    "in_node_snapped": Path("_data/processed/nodes_snapped.gpkg"),
    "out_link_pieces": Path("_data/processed/link_pieces.gpkg"),
}

# Lineage/display attributes reattached onto final pieces via midpoint join
# (see Part D) — same column list 00_data_preparation.qmd uses for the
# original CandidateTDMRoadLinks midpoint transfer.
TRANSFER_COLS = [
    "OBJECTID",
    "UNIQUE_ID",
    "DOT_FCLASS",
    "POSTTYPE",
    "DOT_RTNAME",
    "DOT_HWYNAM",
    "FULLNAME",
    "CARTOCODE",
    "ONEWAY",
    "VERT_LEVEL",  # informational only — see Part D note; not a dissolve/snap/split key
    "SPEED_LMT",
]

# ── CRS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CRS_UTM = "EPSG:26912"  # NAD83 UTM Zone 12N — Utah (metric)
```

---

## Load Data

### Candidate Centerlines

`CandidateTDMRoadLinks.gpkg` (built in `00_data_preparation.qmd`) is already
filtered and dissolved, but it is also pre-cut at arcpy-style junction
points — including incidental boundaries between freeway/ramp/CD rows and
surface-street rows wherever they merely touch, not just at genuine
multi-way branches. Part A below re-dissolves these rows into maximal
chains so that every split point in the final pieces (Part C) comes only
from snapping, not from `CandidateTDMRoadLinks`'s own pre-existing cuts.

```{python}
gdf_centerlines = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_centerlines"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

print(f"Candidate components: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} | CRS: {gdf_centerlines.crs}")
```

### Snapped Nodes

```{python}
gdf_nodes_snapped = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_cc_snapped    = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="cc_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_ext_snapped   = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="ext_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

n_total   = len(gdf_nodes_snapped)
n_snapped = gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
print(f"Nodes: {n_total:,} total | {n_snapped:,} snapped ({n_snapped/n_total:.1%})")
print(f"CC attachment nodes: {len(gdf_cc_snapped):,}")
print(f"External station nodes: {len(gdf_ext_snapped):,}")
```

```{python}
#| eval: false
gdf_nodes_snapped[gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"]].explore()
```

---

## Part A — Full Network Redissolve

`CandidateTDMRoadLinks` is already pre-cut at arcpy-style junction points
(see `00_data_preparation.qmd`'s `rcl_merge`), including boundaries between
freeway/ramp/CD rows and surface-street rows wherever they merely touch —
not just at genuine multi-way branches. To make the final true-shape split
points come **only** from snapped model nodes, every row is re-dissolved
into maximal topological chains (genuine branch points, where 3+ lines
share an endpoint, still remain hard boundaries after dissolve; only
incidental class-boundary splits are undone).

`VERT_LEVEL` isolation is preserved here, but only to prevent a specific
GEOS behavior: `unary_union` on LineStrings doesn't just merge lines that
share an endpoint — it **nodes every crossing point**, inserting a new
vertex (and therefore a new potential break) anywhere two lines cross in
the middle, even when nothing physically connects there. Per-level
isolation is what stops every elevated road from being spuriously noded
against every at-grade street it merely passes over. A same-level-only
merge was verified against a same-network global merge: global dissolve
produced *more* chains (9,368) than even the raw ungrouped candidate rows
(7,642) — i.e. net fragmentation, not consolidation — confirming this is
a real effect at scale here, not a theoretical one. Freeway rows and
surface-street rows are still dissolved together *within* a level — only
the incidental class-boundary splits are undone; genuine branch points (3+
lines sharing an endpoint) remain hard boundaries after dissolve either
way.

```{python}
vert_levels = sorted(gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"].dropna().unique())
print(f"VERT_LEVELs present: {vert_levels}")

fulldissolve_parts = []
for lvl in vert_levels:
    subset = gdf_centerlines[gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"] == lvl]
    if subset.empty:
        continue
    dissolved = dissolve_and_singlepart(subset)
    dissolved["dissolve_level"] = lvl
    print(f"  VERT_LEVEL {lvl}: {len(subset):,} rows -> {len(dissolved):,} dissolved chains")
    fulldissolve_parts.append(dissolved)

gdf_fulldissolve = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    pd.concat(fulldissolve_parts, ignore_index=True),
    geometry="geometry",
    crs=gdf_centerlines.crs,
)
print(f"\nTotal: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} candidate rows -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} redissolved chains")
```

Sanity check: dissolve only merges touching lines into longer chains — it
never adds or removes length. Total length before and after must match.

```{python}
len_before = gdf_centerlines.geometry.length.sum()
len_after = gdf_fulldissolve.geometry.length.sum()
diff_m = abs(len_before - len_after)
print(f"Total length before: {len_before:,.1f} m")
print(f"Total length after:  {len_after:,.1f} m")
print(f"Difference:          {diff_m:.3f} m")
assert diff_m < 1.0, "Redissolve changed total network length — investigate before proceeding."
```

---

## Part B — Resolve Snap Coordinates

`nodes_snapped.gpkg` stores `snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round` rounded to 2 decimal
places (cm precision). Splitting and M-value operations require coordinates that
exactly match a vertex stored in the centerline geometry. For each snapped node,
this step finds the nearest unique centerline vertex within 5 cm and records its
full-precision coordinate.

FixedTransit_Rail nodes are excluded — they snap to GTFS rail infrastructure
(CRT stations, LRT midpoints), not to road centerlines, so they are never road
centerline split points.

```{python}
gdf_nodes_road = gdf_nodes_snapped[
    gdf_nodes_snapped["snap_rule"] != "FixedTransit_Rail"
]
gdf_nodes_resolved = resolve_snap_coords(
    gdf_nodes_road,
    gdf_fulldissolve,
    tolerance=0.05,
)

n_road_snapped = gdf_nodes_road["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
n_resolved     = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"].sum()
n_unresolved   = n_road_snapped - n_resolved
print(f"Coordinate resolution: {n_resolved:,} resolved | {n_unresolved:,} unresolved")
```

```{python}
if n_unresolved > 0:
    unresolved = gdf_nodes_resolved[
        gdf_nodes_resolved["snapped"].fillna(False) & ~gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"]
    ]
    print("Unresolved node sample (check snap quality):")
    print(unresolved[["N", "snap_rule", "snapped_x_round", "snapped_y_round"]].head(10).to_string())
```

Build the list of exact-coordinate Points used as split locations.

```{python}
resolved_mask = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"]
snap_points_exact = [
    Point(row["x_exact"], row["y_exact"])
    for _, row in gdf_nodes_resolved[resolved_mask].iterrows()
]
print(f"Split points prepared: {len(snap_points_exact):,}")
```

---

## Part B2 — Restitch Same-Route VERT_LEVEL Transitions

Part A's per-level dissolve leaves one specific kind of incidental split
behind: where the *same* physical route continues across an elevation
change (e.g. a freeway mainline climbing onto its own flyover), the two
sides were dissolved in different level groups and so remain separate
chains touching at a single point, even though nothing marks a real
boundary there. Since bridges/flyovers have no physical model node where
they rise off the ground, that point would otherwise survive all the way
into the final pieces as a phantom split.

`restitch_vert_level_transitions` finds exactly this pattern — a coordinate
shared by precisely two chain endpoints from two different levels — and
merges the pair only when both sides agree on `DOT_RTNAME` and `POSTTYPE`
(same route, same facility class — e.g. FWY-to-FWY, not a ramp joining the
mainline) at that point, and only when the point isn't itself a snapped
model node (those must stay hard boundaries). Everything else — a
different route merely crossing at a different elevation, a ramp/CD
junction, a genuine 3-way branch — is left split, exactly as before.

```{python}
gdf_fulldissolve_restitched = restitch_vert_level_transitions(
    gdf_fulldissolve,
    "dissolve_level",
    gdf_centerlines,
    "VERT_LEVEL",
    identity_cols=("DOT_RTNAME", "POSTTYPE"),
    exclude_points=snap_points_exact,
    point_tolerance=0.05,
)
attrs = gdf_fulldissolve_restitched.attrs
print(f"Cross-level touch points found: {attrs['n_candidates']:,}")
print(f"  excluded (at a snapped node):     {attrs['n_excluded']:,}")
print(f"  route-identity mismatch (left split): {attrs['n_identity_mismatch']:,}")
print(f"  restitched (same route, merged):  {attrs['n_merged']:,} edges -> {attrs['n_components_merged']:,} chains")
print(f"Chains: {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched):,}")
```

```{python}
len_before = gdf_fulldissolve.geometry.length.sum()
len_after = gdf_fulldissolve_restitched.geometry.length.sum()
diff_m = abs(len_before - len_after)
print(f"Length before: {len_before:,.1f} m | after: {len_after:,.1f} m | diff: {diff_m:.3f} m")
assert diff_m < 1.0, "Restitch changed total network length — investigate before proceeding."
```

---

## Part C — Split at Snapped Nodes

`gdf_fulldissolve_restitched` (Part A + B2) — not the original
`CandidateTDMRoadLinks` rows — is split only at snapped road model-node
positions, so piece boundaries come exclusively from road-node snapping,
never from incidental arcpy junction cuts or an incidental VERT_LEVEL
boundary on the same route. Points that project to within 0.1 mm of a
component's existing endpoint are skipped (already a boundary). After all
splits, each resulting piece is bounded exclusively by:
- a snapped model node position, or
- a genuine branch point or unreconciled route/level boundary already
  present in `gdf_fulldissolve_restitched`.

CC attachment nodes (`cc_nodes_snapped`) and external station nodes
(`ext_nodes_snapped`) are deliberately **not** used as split points here.
`snap_cc_nodes()` computes their position independently (nearest-line
projection from the node's own raw coordinate, uncapped), which can land far
from the node's true location — e.g. a TAZ centroid connector projecting
330 m onto an unrelated freeway mainline — planting a phantom split in the
middle of an otherwise-continuous physical piece. Centroid connector and
external station nodes will be split into the true-shape network as a
separate, later pass instead of being folded into this one.

No lineage keys are carried through this split (`id_cols=()`) — a redissolved
row no longer maps 1:1 to a single original `OBJECTID`. Lineage/display
attributes are reattached afterward via midpoint join (Part D).

```{python}
all_snap_points = snap_points_exact
print(
    f"Split points: {len(snap_points_exact):,} (model nodes). "
    f"CC attachment ({len(gdf_cc_snapped):,}) and external station "
    f"({len(gdf_ext_snapped):,}) nodes excluded — split separately later."
)
```

```{python}
print(f"Splitting {len(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched):,} redissolved chains at {len(all_snap_points):,} points …")
gdf_pieces_split = split_candidate_links(gdf_fulldissolve_restitched, all_snap_points, id_cols=())
print(f"Pieces after split: {len(gdf_pieces_split):,}")
```

---

## Part D — Build Pieces Layer, Reattach Lineage, and Export

Extract start/end endpoint coordinates for each piece (rounded to 2 dp for
matching against `snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round` in the next stage). Since
splitting now runs against the redissolved+restitched
`gdf_fulldissolve_restitched` layer, a piece no longer maps 1:1 to a single
original `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` `OBJECTID` —
lineage/display attributes (`TRANSFER_COLS`) are reattached via the same
midpoint-nearest-join approach `00_data_preparation.qmd` uses to transfer
attributes from raw centerlines onto `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` in the first
place, this time from `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` onto each piece.

```{python}
pieces = gdf_pieces_split.geometry.tolist()
start_coords = np.array([p.coords[0] for p in pieces])
end_coords   = np.array([p.coords[-1] for p in pieces])

gdf_pieces = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "piece_id": np.arange(len(pieces)),
        "x_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "x_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "length_m": np.array([p.length for p in pieces]),
        "geometry": pieces,
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
)
```

`VERT_LEVEL` in the reattached output is informational only — it is the
`VERT_LEVEL` of whichever `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` row lands nearest this
piece's midpoint, nothing more. `VERT_LEVEL` is used upstream only as a
dissolve-grouping key (Part A, to keep GEOS from noding elevated roads
against every at-grade crossing) and as one of two identity checks that
gate a same-route restitch (Part B2, alongside `POSTTYPE`) — it is never
used as a snap-coordinate key, a split key, or in
`03_transfer_attributes.qmd`'s A/B chain matching. A piece can legitimately
span a real elevation change with no split between — e.g. a freeway
climbing onto a flyover — once Part B2 has restitched that specific
transition. In that case the single `VERT_LEVEL` value carried onto the
piece just reflects whichever side of the climb the midpoint happens to
fall on; it is kept for future convenience (e.g. if the true-shape TDM link
output later wants a `VERT_LEVEL` column) and should not be read as
authoritative for the whole piece.

`CandidateTDMRoadLinks` contains a small number of standalone sub-centimetre
"stub" features (max ~6 mm, confirmed by direct `OBJECTID` lookup) — digitizing
artifacts, not anything this pipeline creates. Because `split_candidate_links`
never cuts a component shorter than its 0.5 m `_EPS`, each stub passes through
whole as its own piece; since both of its (near-identical) endpoints round to
the same snapped-node coordinate, Stage 3 later resolves `A_piece == B_piece`
for it — a spurious self-loop. Genuine physical loop roads (cloverleaf/collector
loops that legitimately start and end at the same point) are tens of metres to
several kilometres long, so a `length_m < 1 m` gate removes only the artifacts.

```{python}
n_before_drop = len(gdf_pieces)
degenerate_mask = (
    (gdf_pieces["x_start"] == gdf_pieces["x_end"])
    & (gdf_pieces["y_start"] == gdf_pieces["y_end"])
    & (gdf_pieces["length_m"] < 1.0)
)
n_degenerate = int(degenerate_mask.sum())
gdf_pieces = gdf_pieces[~degenerate_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
print(
    f"Dropped {n_degenerate:,} / {n_before_drop:,} degenerate zero-length pieces "
    f"(start == end, length < 1 m) — pre-existing near-duplicate-vertex stub "
    f"features already present as standalone rows in CandidateTDMRoadLinks, "
    f"not created by this pipeline. Real closed-loop roads (cloverleaf/collector "
    f"loops, tens of metres to several km long) are left untouched — the length "
    f"gate cleanly separates the two populations with a >3,000x margin."
)

gdf_pieces = transfer_attributes_by_midpoint(gdf_pieces, gdf_centerlines, TRANSFER_COLS)

n_null = gdf_pieces[TRANSFER_COLS].isna().any(axis=1).sum()
print(f"Pieces with a null transferred attribute: {n_null:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

PATHS["out_link_pieces"].parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf_pieces.to_file(PATHS["out_link_pieces"], driver="GPKG")
print(f"Exported {len(gdf_pieces):,} pieces → {PATHS['out_link_pieces']}")
```
